text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH on service `inference-latency-prod` (INC-2026-314). Trigger: 1m p95 latency > 800ms in us-west-2 canary.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-314 created and notified rotation.

riley: saw the page, on it. checking dashboards now.

jamie: I briefly saw a spike on the canary graphs a min ago. might be canary noise, can we confirm impact?

riley: looking at prod traffic — overall qps steady, 5xxs not elevated. canary p95 spiked on a single host group (proxy-proxy-7).

sophie: pinging infra logs for that host group, pulling `kubectl logs` and proxy traces.

riley: commands: 
```
# check host metrics
rollups query --metric=http_proxy_latency --filter=host:proxy-proxy-7 --range=5m
# quick check for OOMs
kubectl get pods -l role=proxy -o wide | grep proxy-proxy-7
```

jamie: infra-alerts shows a brief CPU burst on proxy-proxy-7 at +00:00:18 that lines up with the latency blip. no container restarts.

incident-bot: Auto-escalation scheduled in 5 minutes if not acknowledged.

riley: acked the PD incident (INC-2026-314) and added note "investigating canary-only p95 spike, no customer 5xx increase".

sophie: pulled proxy thread dumps, nothing stuck. network path flapped for ~30s according to vpc flow logs — small burst of retries to a downstream redis shard.

jamie: that correlates. looks like transient network congestion between the proxy AZ and redis zone C. cache miss climb but service degraded only for that canary set.

riley: mitigation — temporarily redirecting canary traffic away from proxy-proxy-7 and scaling proxy pool +1 to soak. running command now: `infractl adjust-asg proxy-asg +1 --reason "canary isolate"`

ops-manager: thanks, keep me posted. any customer-facing impact?

riley: early check: no increase in error budgets or SLA alerts. internal canary flag tripped but only for synthetic runs. marking customer_impact: none.

incident-bot: PD incident INC-2026-314 status changed to "acknowledged" by riley.

(30s pass)

jamie: proxy-asg scaled and new instances warmed. retries dropped, canary p95 trending back to baseline.

sophie: vpc flow logs show the congestion cleared at +00:01:20.

riley: I'll close the PD incident once the canary stays stable for two consecutive checks (2m).

(90s later)

jamie: canary steady. p95 back to normal for 3 checks.

riley: closing INC-2026-314 — root cause: transient inter-AZ network congestion impacting a single proxy host group, caused a short-lived canary latency spike. no customer impact. remediation: isolated canary away from affected host, scaled proxy pool, and network team alerted to trace inter-AZ path. follow-up: ops postmortem thread to add later if we see recurrence.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-314 resolved (auto-resolution not required).

ops-manager: nice quick triage, thanks all. riley — can you add a short note to oncall log with the commands run and metrics you checked?

riley: done — added to oncall log and created follow-up ticket INFRA-927 for deeper network traces.

jamie: thumbs up :thumbsup:

sophie: back to watch — no further alerts.

riley: handing off to jamie in 5 min, I'm stepping out for a quick break but monitor is green.

jamie: got it, I'll keep an eye.

(End of thread)
